meta.purpose: Explain onboarding support available to prospective GPs — what the practice can assist with, what it cannot approve, and what depends on external agencies.

disclaimer.short: This matrix describes practice support for onboarding conversations. It is not a guarantee of placement, eligibility, Medicare outcomes, or start dates.
disclaimer.full: Woolloongabba Medical Centre shares this capability matrix so prospective GPs can understand how we support onboarding. Support is practical and collaborative. We do not issue Medicare provider numbers, determine DPA or Health Insurance Act s19AB outcomes, approve visas or work rights, or provide legal or migration advice. External agencies make their own decisions on their timelines. Nothing in this matrix constitutes an offer of employment or a commercial commitment.

canAssist.label: What WMC can assist with
canAssist.description: Practical practice support we may provide during onboarding preparation and early weeks, subject to mutual agreement and capacity.

cannotApprove.label: What WMC cannot approve
cannotApprove.description: Decisions, credentials, or outcomes the practice does not control and must not imply it can grant.

externalDepends.label: What depends on external agencies
externalDepends.description: Steps that rely on Services Australia, AHPRA, colleges, indemnity insurers, Department of Home Affairs, or other external bodies.

categories.label: Provider number support
categories.doctorFacingSummary: We help you prepare accurate practice details for your Services Australia application. We do not issue or approve provider numbers.
canAssist: Share verified practice name, address, and location identifiers needed for a location-linked provider number application
Explain the difference between an existing provider number and a location-specific number for this practice
Coordinate timing so onboarding documents and start planning remain aligned while you await Services Australia correspondence
Point you to official Services Australia resources and our Provider Number Readiness checklist
cannotApprove: Issuing, allocating, or guaranteeing a Medicare provider number
Approving a provider number application on your behalf as the decision-maker
Confirming that a number will be granted by a particular date
Overriding Services Australia processing outcomes

externalDepends.dependency: Issues Medicare provider numbers and processes applications
Lodges and tracks the application; holds responsibility for accuracy of personal details

categories.typicalTiming: Before go-live billing; ideally completed or well advanced before first patient session

categories.label: Medicare onboarding guidance
categories.doctorFacingSummary: We orient you to how Medicare billing is handled in this practice. We do not determine your individual Medicare eligibility or billing rights.
canAssist: Walk through local Medicare billing workflows used at Woolloongabba Medical Centre
Explain practice preferences for item selection documentation, bulk-billing pathways where used, and private billing coordination
Share practice contact points for billing questions during early sessions
Flag common documentation habits that support accurate claiming in everyday general practice
cannotApprove: Determining whether you are personally eligible to bill Medicare for specific services
Approving exemptions, restrictions, or Health Insurance Act arrangements
Guaranteeing claim acceptance or payment outcomes
Providing formal Medicare advice as a substitute for Services Australia

externalDepends.dependency: Medicare rules, provider arrangements, and claim processing
Clinical judgement and responsibility for items claimed under your provider number

categories.typicalTiming: Orientation week and first consulting fortnight

categories.label: Orientation
categories.doctorFacingSummary: A structured introduction to the practice, policies, rooms, emergency processes, and day-to-day expectations.
canAssist: Schedule a practice orientation covering layout, emergency procedures, privacy, and key contacts
Introduce clinic hours, after-hours arrangements, and escalation pathways
Provide access to relevant practice policies once onboarding is mutually confirmed
Clarify how feedback and clinical governance conversations usually work here
cannotApprove: Substituting orientation for external registration or credentialing requirements
Waiving mandatory professional obligations (AHPRA, indemnity, working rights)
Guaranteeing a start date before documents and mutual agreement are complete

externalDepends.dependency: Current registration status remains a prerequisite for clinical practice
Adequate professional indemnity cover for the intended start period

categories.typicalTiming: Before or at first consulting week

categories.label: Clinical software onboarding
categories.doctorFacingSummary: Hands-on familiarisation with clinical records, prescribing, results, and documentation used at this practice.
canAssist: Provide supervised walkthrough of clinical software used at the practice
Demonstrate common workflows: notes, results, recalls, referrals, and prescribing patterns used locally
Arrange login credentials once identity and onboarding checks are complete
Offer early-week support contacts for software questions
cannotApprove: Certifying external software competencies beyond practice use
Granting system access before required identity and onboarding checks
Guaranteeing that prior software experience will transfer without orientation

externalDepends.dependency: Account provisioning, licensing, and technical availability
Completes orientation and asks for clarification on unfamiliar workflows

categories.label: Nursing introductions
categories.doctorFacingSummary: Meet the nursing team and understand how treatment-room, preventive, and care-coordination support works alongside GP consulting.
canAssist: Introduce you to nursing team members and their usual scopes of support
Explain how treatment-room activity, vaccinations, and care coordination are requested in practice
Clarify communication preferences for same-day clinical support
Share how nursing cover relates to session planning and room use
cannotApprove: Promising dedicated nursing support for every session regardless of cover
Expanding nursing scope beyond practice protocols and professional standards
Guaranteeing staffing levels that depend on roster capacity

externalDepends.dependency: Day-to-day nursing availability is subject to roster and leave

categories.label: Reception workflows
categories.doctorFacingSummary: Understand how appointments, arrivals, messaging, and patient flow are coordinated at reception.
canAssist: Explain appointment booking patterns, HotDoc online booking, and how sessions appear to patients
Introduce reception contacts for messages, results follow-up, and day-of changes
Clarify expectations for running late, urgent add-ons, and communication with waiting patients
Walk through how new patients and returning patients are usually registered
cannotApprove: Changing whole-of-practice booking policy unilaterally for one doctor without agreement
Guaranteeing a particular patient volume or case-mix
Bypassing privacy and identity verification steps at reception

externalDepends.dependency: Online booking availability and patient-facing slots
Attendance patterns and preference for online versus phone booking

categories.label: Practice systems
categories.doctorFacingSummary: An overview of privacy, recalls, quality processes, pathology/radiology preferences, and everyday operational systems.
canAssist: Orient you to privacy, records, and information-handling expectations at the practice
Explain recall and reminder approaches used for preventive care
Share preferred pathology and radiology workflows used locally
Introduce quality and accreditation touchpoints relevant to consulting GPs
cannotApprove: Waiving privacy or records obligations
Approving external accreditation on behalf of the practice without process
Guaranteeing that every system preference matches every previous practice you have worked in

externalDepends.dependency: Ordering portals, result delivery, and local service arrangements
Practice accreditation cycles and evidence requirements

categories.label: Session planning
categories.doctorFacingSummary: Collaborative planning of consulting days and hours based on rooms, nursing cover, and practice need — not a marketplace listing.
canAssist: Discuss preferred session patterns (days, part-time, staged growth) against current capacity
Explain how room availability and nursing cover influence what can be offered
Document a draft session plan for mutual review before go-live
Review early adjustments once patient demand and team fit are clearer
cannotApprove: Guaranteeing a fixed session template before capacity and mutual agreement are confirmed
Promising patient volumes, earnings, or fill rates
Overriding safety or coverage limits to add sessions

externalDepends.dependency: Rooms, nursing cover, and existing GP session commitments
Availability, start timing, and preference clarity

categories.label: Team integration
categories.doctorFacingSummary: Introductions to GPs and the wider team, and practical support for settling into collaborative care.
canAssist: Introduce you to consulting GPs and key non-clinical team members
Explain how internal clinical questions and collegial support usually work
Include you in relevant team communications once you have started
Invite feedback on early weeks so small friction points can be addressed
cannotApprove: Guaranteeing a particular mentoring relationship without mutual agreement
Substituting collegial support for formal supervision where a training pathway requires it
Promising an immediate full patient list or established continuity panel

externalDepends.dependency: Where applicable, formal registrar supervision and training requirements
Who is present on your consulting days

crossCuttingPrinciples: Support is offered in good faith and subject to practice capacity.
External agency decisions are independent of Woolloongabba Medical Centre.
No public guarantees of eligibility, income, patient volume, or start dates.
Language remains practice-voice: clear, calm, and free of recruitment-agency framing.
Doctors remain responsible for their registration, indemnity, work rights, and Medicare applications.
